goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/components/badges.css.scss:55 — Converts already-working plain CSS `display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline;` into the new mixins, adding an indirection layer and creating two competing flex patterns (raw vs. mixin) in the codebase

adjudication.rationale: The diff does replace `display: inline-flex;` and `align-items: baseline;` in `badges.css.scss` with `@include inline-flex();` and `@include align-items(baseline);`, but the diff also adds these mixins (with vendor-prefixed outputs) and uses them elsewhere, indicating a deliberate refactor toward mixins rather than creating a review-worthy problem. The claim about "two competing flex patterns" cannot be verified from this diff alone (it doesn’t show other remaining raw flex usages), and the rest is largely a style/indirection preference, not a concrete defect or actionable issue grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:98 — Hand-rolled vendor-prefixed mixins may duplicate an existing autoprefixer/build-tool prefixing solution already used in the project, risking two redundant prefixing mechanisms long-term

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add new hand-rolled vendor-prefixed flexbox mixins in `mixins.scss` and updates call sites to use them, but nothing in the provided diff shows whether the project already uses Autoprefixer or another build-time prefixing tool. The finding hinges on an external project configuration not visible here, so it’s speculative rather than verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss:14 — .title { float: left; }` is deleted outright rather than migrated, merging its intent into the unrelated `.contents` flex rule and leaving any `.title` element without dedicated styling

adjudication.rationale: The diff does delete the `.title { float: left; }` rule in `header.scss`, and instead makes `.contents` a flex container with centered alignment. However, from the diff alone it’s not verifiable that this is a problem: in a flex container, a `.title` element would naturally lay out at the start without needing `float: left`, so the intent may be implicitly preserved. The claim that the intent was merged into an “unrelated” rule and that `.title` is left in a broken state is speculative beyond what the diff shows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:278 — Unrelated spacing/margin changes (padding, margin-top, paragraph margin) are bundled into a diff framed as a "flexbox mixin" performance change, increasing review difficulty and regression risk

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss`, the change adds flexbox (`@include flexbox();`, `@include align-items(center);`) to `.small-action`, but it also modifies layout/spacing independently: `.small-action-desc` padding changes from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` (and removes `margin-top: 5px`) to `padding: 0 1.5%`, `p { margin: 5px 0; }` becomes `margin: 0;`, and `> p` removes `padding-top: 4px`. These are real, diff-grounded changes that are not strictly required by introducing the flexbox mixins and do increase review surface/regression risk by bundling concerns.
